calendar_note: Every date in this record is synthetic and belongs to the hypothetical Project Northcell. No organisation, plant, vehicle, technician or recycler named here exists.
purpose: Establish what a release of this item is, how that release is identified unambiguously, and what a recipient must be able to determine from the identification alone. A release that cannot be identified cannot be recalled, and an item whose configuration cannot be recalled cannot be serviced.

in_scope: Software configuration: application, bootloader and the commissioning tool
Hardware: board revision and the component set fitted to it
Data: the safe-operating-area limit set and the calibration data
Documentation: the set of documents shipped with the release
out_of_scope: The pack, which is configured and identified by the pack integrator against this item, not by this item's release
The vehicle, which has its own configuration identification
Any statement that the released configuration is safe: this record identifies a configuration, it does not qualify one

responsible_roles.responsibility: Owns the release decision and the release record
Produces the content manifest and the identification string
Confirms that the release checklist in this record is complete
Confirms the board revision and component set

procedures.action: Freeze the software build and record its content hash, its build configuration and its compiler and linker versions
procedures.acceptance_condition: The recorded hash matches the hash of the artefact that will be shipped, and the build is reproducible from the recorded configuration
procedures.decision_point: The build is declared reproducible or it is not released

procedures.action: Record the hardware configuration: board revision, the fitted component set and any component substitutions permitted for this variant
procedures.acceptance_condition: Every component on a safety-relevant path is named with its part number and its variant eligibility
procedures.decision_point: Whether a proposed substitution is eligible

procedures.action: Record the data configuration: the safe-operating-area limit set, the sensor tables and the calibration values, each with the parameter id that owns it
procedures.acceptance_condition: Every limit value resolves to a parameter in the canonical parameter registry and no value appears here that does not
procedures.decision_point: Whether the limit set may differ from the baselined set

procedures.action: Generate the configuration identification string from the content of steps 1 to 3 and record it on the physical item and in the non-volatile memory
procedures.acceptance_condition: The string on the item can be read back and resolves to exactly one configuration
procedures.decision_point: Whether the item may ship with an identification that cannot be read back

procedures.action: Complete the release checklist: verification status of every requirement, open finding count by severity, change records included, and the safety case review record
procedures.acceptance_condition: No critical or high finding is open against any released record, and every unexecuted verification is named with the reason it is unexecuted
procedures.decision_point: Whether the release proceeds with unexecuted verification

procedures.action: Publish the release notes stating what changed, what was re-verified, what was not and why, and what a recipient must do differently
procedures.acceptance_condition: The 'what was not and why' section is populated and is not empty; a release note that lists only successes is a marketing document

configuration_identification.identification_scheme: One identification string per released configuration, formed from the content hashes of the software items and the canonical identifiers of the hardware and data items. The string is written to the item's non-volatile memory at the end of the line and read back before the item is allowed to leave. A readback that does not resolve to exactly one configuration is a line stop. In this corpus the scheme is described and nothing has been written or read: no item exists.

interactions_with_other_lifecycle_areas.interaction: The identification is written and read back on the production line
interactions_with_other_lifecycle_areas.consequence_if_the_interaction_is_broken: An item ships with an identification nobody verified, which is the failure the readback step exists to prevent.

interactions_with_other_lifecycle_areas.interaction: The calibration record is part of the configuration identification
interactions_with_other_lifecycle_areas.consequence_if_the_interaction_is_broken: An item is identified as one configuration and programmed as another, and the identification becomes actively misleading.

interactions_with_other_lifecycle_areas.interaction: The service class reads the identification to determine what is fitted
interactions_with_other_lifecycle_areas.consequence_if_the_interaction_is_broken: A service action is performed against a configuration the technician did not know was fitted.

interactions_with_other_lifecycle_areas.interaction: Field data is keyed by the identification string
interactions_with_other_lifecycle_areas.consequence_if_the_interaction_is_broken: A field event cannot be attributed to a configuration and the event analysis produces a trend that mixes configurations.

operational_authorisation_statement: This record is a fictional engineering artefact. It is NOT an authorised release procedure, it grants no production authority, and no step in it has been performed. The release it describes has not happened. production_authorized is false and human_approval_status is pending on every record it would release.

evidence_state.reason: No production line, vehicle, charging site, workshop, fleet or recycling facility exists anywhere in this corpus. Master-prompt clause 2.5 forbids energising hardware and connecting to vehicles, so no step below can be performed by any means available here. The record documents the procedure and records that it has not been run.

limitations: Synthetic. The release described has not occurred and no item exists to release.
The identification scheme is described and not demonstrated. No readback has been performed and no string has been resolved.

The real foxBMS source demonstrates a release version history (docs/general/releases.csv), and that history is the only real basis for any release process claim. It is a version history, not a release plan or a release checklist, and this record does not claim the real project performs any of these steps.

The release checklist in step 5 requires a safety case review record. The corpus has one, and it is a skeleton with no evidence behind it, so on this corpus's own terms the release checklist could not be completed.
